source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 2 November 1946, p. 5 ("Rural Council elections")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Unopposed new members from the Belfast News-Letter (18 October 1946, p. 6) and Derry Journal (18 October 1946, p. 7).

note: Triennial election of Limavady rural district (23 divisions); Co. Londonderry polled 31 October 1946. Seven divisions were contested; six new members and ten retiring councillors were returned unopposed (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 October 1946, p. 6). The Sentinel of 2 November 1946, p. 5, prints the results and the full new council of 23 names, without divisions; the Nationalists won control for the first time. Seven of the retiring members' divisions are taken from the 1939 return, as each contest note says. Faughanvale added and the six unopposed new members re-cited (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Glendinning was the outgoing member.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Drumreighland' to Drumraighland (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (DRUMRAIGHLAND) spell it Drumraighland. This round was filed under the spelling 'Drumreighland', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (drumreighland) answers with a redirect to this one.
